page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It is configured with 1 dedicated vCPU based on the arm64 CPU architecture and is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware accelerators, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Operating on an arm64 architecture with a dedicated CPU allocation, the c4a-standard-1 offers predictable compute resources for entry-level workloads. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the arm64 architecture typically provides a favorable performance-per-resource profile, making this instance suitable for resource-constrained environments that do not require x86 compatibility or high-density memory configurations. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration limits its utility for data-intensive or parallel computing tasks. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, such as microservices, small-scale web serving, development environments, and basic utility scripting.
